subject: Order form: surcharge carveout & pricing-smoothing language
messages:
From: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@helixanalytics.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-18 09:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form draft (redline attached)

Markus —

Thanks for sending the latest order form. Procurement attached our redline (Helix_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf). Two items we want to highlight up front so you can flag with legal: 

- Surcharge carveout: we need an explicit exemption for our usage spikes tied to batch inference jobs — the original surcharge language would effectively double price for those cases.
- Pricing smoothing / floor: we propose a smoothing clause so that month-to-month unit-price volatility greater than 30% triggers a reconciliation rather than immediate step changes.

Can you confirm whether Redwood would accept a temporary surcharge exemption for the first 90 days post-go-live and agree to the smoothing reconciliation approach?

We need this resolved before the procurement committee meets on 8/25.

Thanks,
Jordan
Procurement, Helix Analytics

Attachments: Helix_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf (application/pdf, 98KB)

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear redline and the two flags. Looping in Marissa (sales lead), Neha (finance), and Jonas (legal) to get alignment quickly. High level from our side:

- We can consider a limited surcharge exemption for an initial ramp period, but we need guardrails to avoid open-ended exposure.
- Pricing smoothing sounds reasonable as a reconciliation mechanism, but language matters (timing, lookback window, and whether credits or true-up invoices).

Jonas / legal — can you review the attached redline and propose precise exhibit/paragraph edits that would give Helix comfort while protecting Redwood? Suggested outputs: 1) 90-day temporary surcharge carveout language; 2) smoothing clause with a 3-month lookback and true-up credit.

Jordan — we'll aim to get proposed edits back by end-of-day 8/19 so you have time before your committee.

Best,

Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-19 09:33 -0700
Subject: RE: Order form draft (redline attached)

Team —

I reviewed Helix's redline and drafted two narrow edits that should be defensible and acceptable:

1) Temporary surcharge carveout (90 days):
- Proposed text: "For the initial 90 days following Production Launch, Customer shall not be assessed Surcharges under Section 4.3 for usage categorized as scheduled batch inference jobs provided Customer notifies Redwood in writing at least 48 hours prior to scheduled batch windows. Surcharges may resume after the 90-day period subject to Section 4.3 as amended by any subsequent written agreement."
- Rationale: limits exposure, requires scheduling notice to prevent surprise spikes.

2) Pricing smoothing / reconciliation:
- Proposed text: "If the Customer's effective per-unit pricing for an invoice month deviates by more than thirty percent (30%) from the three-month rolling average of effective per-unit pricing, the Parties shall perform a reconciliation. If the deviation results in Customer overpayment, Redwood will issue a credit on the next invoice; if underpayment, Redwood may invoice the difference. Reconciliation requests must be submitted within sixty (60) days of the invoice date."
- Rationale: provides a predictable reconciliation process and a firm lookback/window.

Other notes: Avoid open-ended carveouts tied to "spikes" without definition — that will create billing disputes. Also propose adding an examples appendix to Exhibit B showing how smoothing and credits are calculated (simple arithmetic examples).

I can produce a tracked-change version of Exhibit B tonight. Do we want to send that straight to Jordan or to Marissa/Markus for review first?

Jonas
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: (in-draft) RWI_Proposed_ExhibitB_smoothing_v2.docx

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@helixanalytics.com>

Jordan —

Thanks for the patience. Please find our proposed edits attached (RWI_Proposed_ExhibitB_smoothing_v2.docx) and summarized below: 

- 90-day surcharge carveout for scheduled batch inference jobs, with 48-hour advance notice required.
- 3-month rolling-average smoothing clause with a 60-day reconciliation window; credits applied to the next invoice if overpayment is found.
- Added an examples appendix to Exhibit B illustrating the math for common scenarios.

High-level ask from Helix: confirm acceptance or provide any redlines to our proposed language by COB 8/21 so we can finalize commercial terms for signature. If helpful, I'm happy to join a 30-minute call on 8/20 to walk the language with your procurement and legal.

Regards,
Markus
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RWI_Proposed_ExhibitB_smoothing_v2.docx, Pricing_Exhibit_Summary.xlsx

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the concrete language. Helix can accept the 90-day carveout for scheduled batch jobs and the 3-month rolling reconciliation as written, with one small tweak: we ask that the 48-hour notice be waived for the first 30 days of the 90-day ramp (we have a couple of immediate migrations and can't always schedule windows that far in advance).

If you can accept that tweak, we are good to finalize commercial terms and move to DocuSign. We aim to sign by 8/25.

Jordan
